name: ui-lib
description: React component library. Next.js, TypeScript, CSS variables + CSS Modules. Controls are built on Base UI.
principles: HTML first: use the semantic element for the job. Own components render correct HTML; Base UI components handle behavior and ARIA.
Use semantic tokens only; never hardcode colors, spacing or fonts.
Every control needs an accessible name: Field `label`, the component's `label`/`legend`, or `aria-label`.
One way to do each thing: links are Link, actions are Button, headings are Heading, body text is Text.
Keep heading levels in order, one h1 per page.

components.name: Text
components.description:
Body-level text: paragraphs, labels, captions and inline code.
For headings use `Heading`; for links use `Link`.
components.renders: p (body variants), span (label, caption), code (code); or the element in `as`
components.composition: `as` accepts only: p, span, label, strong, em, small, div, code. No links or buttons.
components.whenToUse: Any paragraph, label, caption or inline code that is not a heading. Small styles: `label` for controls (buttons, tabs); `body-sm` for secondary reading text (descriptions, helper text); `caption` for metadata (timestamps, counters, footnotes).
avoid: Headings: use Heading.
Links: use Link.
Actions: use Button.
Setting font-size or color by hand.
Caption size="sm" (10px) for lowercase running text: it is intentional for uppercase metadata, where the extra tracking keeps it legible.
Form labels: use Label, or Field when you also need description and error.
components.accessibility: Do not use tone="subtle" for required text.

props.name: as
props.description:
HTML element to render. Defaults by variant: `p` for body variants, `span` for
`label` and `caption`, `code` for `code`.

props.name: casing
props.description: Set to `uppercase` for small uppercase captions.

props.name: hyphenate
props.description: Allow the browser to hyphenate words when the line needs to break.

props.name: lineClamp
props.description: Clamp direct text content to this many lines. Do not use on elements containing nested HTML.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size within the variant: body is 18px (`lg`), 15px (`base`) or 13px (`sm`); caption is 12px, 11px or 10px;
code is 14px (`base`), 13px (`sm`) or 12px (`xs`). Ignored by `label` and `emphasis`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Text color from the semantic color tokens.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Keep one line and show an ellipsis when the text does not fit.

props.name: variant
props.description: Which text style to apply. Appearance only; it does not change the element.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight. Only three exist; there is no light. Defaults to the variant's own weight.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Text>Default paragraph.</Text>
<Text size="lg">Large body text</Text>
<Text variant="caption" tone="muted">Helper text</Text>
<Text lineClamp={2}>A long description that can safely truncate...</Text>

components.name: Link
components.description:
A link for navigation. It renders an `a`, or the component given to `LinkProvider` (such as `next/link`).
Links with a label always show an underline so they do not rely on color alone. For actions that do not navigate, use `Button`.
Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon`. An icon on its own is a valid link (`startIcon` + `aria-label`).
components.renders: a
components.composition: Native anchor props pass through. `href` is required. Put a trailing icon in `endIcon` (no `size`). Set `standalone` for a link used as a standalone action; inline links in a sentence stay inline. For a link styled as a button, use `Button` with `href`.
components.whenToUse: Navigation to another page, section or resource, inline in text.
avoid: Actions that do not navigate: use Button with onClick.
Links without visible text.
Button-styled navigation: use Button with href.
components.accessibility: Always underlined so it does not rely on color (the underline gets stronger on hover). Use `target="_blank"` only with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes. Required: a link without `href` is not a link.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the link sizes it.

props.name: standalone
props.description: Marks a standalone action link (not inline in a sentence) so it gets a 44px hit area on touch devices.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the link sizes it.

props.name: tone
props.description: `default` uses the text color, `muted` the secondary text color, `inherit` the surrounding color. The underline is always there.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Link href="/docs">Read the docs</Link>
<Link href="/docs" endIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />}>Read the docs</Link>
<Link href="/next" aria-label="Next page" startIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />} />

components.name: Kbd
components.description: A keyboard key or shortcut. Renders a native `kbd`. Use one `Kbd` per key and join keys with text.
components.renders: kbd
components.composition: One Kbd per key; join keys with text such as +.
components.whenToUse: Keyboard shortcuts in docs and UI.
avoid: Using it as a button.
components.accessibility: Native kbd semantics. Spell out symbols that screen readers read poorly, for example add VisuallyHidden text.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size of the key.

props.name: variant
props.description: Surface treatment.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>

components.name: Badge
components.description:
Small status, category or count label. Text is always the primary signal; the
variant only reinforces it.

Keep the text to one or two words and truncate counts to two digits (`99+`).
Badges are secondary and supportive: never use one as a heading or a key
indicator. Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon`; they follow the badge size: sm 12px, md 16px,
lg 20px. An icon-only badge needs `aria-label`; it then renders with `role="img"`.
components.renders: span, or the element passed in `render`
components.composition: Text children, plus optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`); never put icons in children. `loading` adds a spinner (`spinnerPosition`: start or end). `variant`: default, inverted, outline, brand, success or danger. Pass `render={<Link href="…" />}` to render a link. Keep text to one or two words; truncate counts to two digits (`99+`).
components.whenToUse: Short status or count labels next to other content.
avoid: Using color as the only signal: always include text.
Badges as headings or key indicators: they are secondary and supportive.
Long descriptions: badges are for short labels.
Styling a badge like a button when it acts as one: use Button.
components.accessibility: Meaning must be in the text; the variant only reinforces it. A badge rendered as a link keeps the link's own accessible name.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the badge sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner before or after the text, for statuses still in progress.

props.name: render
props.description:
Renders the badge as another element or component, e.g. a link:
`render={<Link href="/docs" />}`. Keyboard and focus behavior then come from
that element, since Base UI merges the props.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner shape: `pill` (fully round) or `rounded` (small radius).

props.name: size
props.description: Height and type scale: `sm` 20px, `md` 24px, `lg` 28px.

props.name: spinnerPosition
props.description: Side the spinner sits on.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the badge sizes it.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual treatment. `default` is a quiet component surface, `inverted` a filled
high-contrast pill, `outline` only an inset ring, and `brand`, `success` and
`danger` are soft semantic tints (translucent background, colored text).

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Badge>Default</Badge>
<Badge variant="inverted">Inverted</Badge>
<Badge variant="outline">Outline</Badge>
<Badge variant="brand">Brand</Badge>
<Badge variant="success">Success</Badge>
<Badge variant="danger">Danger</Badge>
<Badge variant="success" startIcon={<CheckIcon />}>Success</Badge>
<Badge render={<a href="#link" />}>Open link</Badge>

components.name: DescriptionList
components.description: Semantic `dl` structure for terms and descriptions. It does not impose a data model.
components.renders: dl with native dt/dd children
components.composition: Compose `DescriptionListTerm` and `DescriptionListDetails` in alternating pairs. `layout` is `stacked`, `inline` or `horizontal`; `narrow` reduces the horizontal label column.
components.whenToUse: Semantic term/description content such as metadata, settings or record details.
avoid: Using a div-based grid for term/value semantics.
Putting unrelated content into one list.
components.accessibility: Uses native description-list semantics; keep each term paired with its following description.

props.name: children
props.description: Term and detail children, normally alternating `DescriptionListTerm` and `DescriptionListDetails`.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout for the term/detail pairs.

props.name: narrow
props.description: Uses a narrower label column in `horizontal` layout.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: DescriptionListTerm
parts.description: A term inside `DescriptionList`.
parts.composition: Child of `DescriptionList`; accepts native dt props.
parts.whenToUse: The name or term in a description list.
avoid: Using it outside a description list.
parts.accessibility: Native term semantics.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: DescriptionListDetails
parts.description: A description/value inside `DescriptionList`.
parts.composition: Child of `DescriptionList`; accepts native dd props.
parts.whenToUse: The description or value paired with a term.
avoid: Using it outside a description list.
parts.accessibility: Native description semantics.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: NameValueList
components.description: Data-driven name/value presentation built on native description-list semantics.
components.renders: dl with generated dt/dd pairs
components.composition: Pass `items` with `label` and `value`, then choose `layout` (`stacked`, `inline` or `horizontal`).
components.whenToUse: Data-driven name/value pairs where a semantic description list is appropriate.
avoid: Using it when each value needs custom structural markup; use DescriptionList directly.
Using it for tabular data; use Table.
components.accessibility: Renders native description-list semantics for every item.

props.name: items
props.description: Data pairs to render as `dt`/`dd`.

props.name: layout
props.description: Visual arrangement of the pairs.

props.name: narrow
props.description: Uses a narrower label column in `horizontal` layout.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Stack
components.description:
One-dimensional layout: children in a row or column with a token-based gap.

`direction` and `gap` accept a per-breakpoint object. Breakpoints are mobile-first:
`sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem, `xl` 80rem. A missing breakpoint inherits the
smaller one, so `{ md: "row" }` stays `column` below 48rem.
components.renders: div (or `as`) with display:flex
components.composition: `as="ul"` or `"ol"` requires `li` children.
components.whenToUse: Arranging children in one direction with a consistent gap.
avoid: Two-dimensional layouts: use Grid.
Margins between children: use `gap`.
components.accessibility: List semantics are restored with role="list" because removing markers drops them in some screen readers.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment on the cross axis. Accepts per-breakpoint values.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. With `ul` or `ol`, children must be `li` elements.

props.name: direction
props.description:
Main axis. `column` stacks vertically. Pass a per-breakpoint object to change it responsively;
mobile-first, a missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.

props.name: gap
props.description:
Space between children, from the spacing scale. Pass a per-breakpoint object to change it
responsively; mobile-first, a missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.

props.name: justify
props.description: Distribution on the main axis. Accepts per-breakpoint values.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets children wrap onto new lines.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
Title Body
  • One
  • Two
    •  One Two

components.name: Grid
components.description:
Two-dimensional layout using CSS grid with a token-based gap.

Breakpoints are mobile-first: `sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem, `xl` 80rem.
A missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.
components.renders: div (or `as`) with display:grid
components.composition: `columns` is a number (equal columns), a full grid-template-columns string, or a per-breakpoint object. `minColumnWidth` uses automatic columns and overrides `columns`.
components.whenToUse: Two-dimensional layouts and card grids.
avoid: One-dimensional layouts: use Stack.
components.accessibility: Visual order should match DOM order.
choosing: Cards, tiles and galleries: use `minColumnWidth` (for example `"16rem"`). Columns fit automatically, with no breakpoints.
Fixed layouts that change by screen (sidebar plus content, 1/2/3 columns): use the responsive `columns` object, for example `{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }`.
Unequal columns: pass a string such as `"2fr 1fr"`, optionally per breakpoint, for example `{ base: 1, lg: "2fr 1fr" }`.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of items inside their cells on the block axis. Accepts per-breakpoint values.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. With `ul` or `ol`, children must be `li` elements.

props.name: columnGap
props.description: Column gap override.

props.name: columns
gap
props.description:
Space between rows and columns, from the spacing scale. Pass a per-breakpoint object
to change it responsively; mobile-first, a missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.

props.name: justify
props.description: Alignment of items inside their cells on the inline axis. Accepts per-breakpoint values.

props.name: minColumnWidth
props.description:
Minimum width for automatic columns, for example `"16rem"`. Uses `auto-fit` with no
breakpoints and overrides `columns`. `min(100%, X)` prevents overflow on narrow screens.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Row gap override.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Grid columns={3} gap="4">...</Grid>
<Grid columns="2fr 1fr">...</Grid>
<Grid minColumnWidth="16rem" gap="4">...</Grid>
<Grid columns={{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }} gap={{ base: "3", md: "6" }}>...</Grid>
<Grid columns={{ base: 1, lg: "2fr 1fr" }} align="start" justify={{ base: "stretch", md: "center" }}>...</Grid>

components.name: Container
components.description: Centers content, constrains its readable width and applies responsive horizontal gutters.
components.renders: div (or `as`) with a centered max width and horizontal gutters
components.composition: `size` selects a semantic container width (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`) and `gutter` selects responsive horizontal padding from the spacing scale.
components.whenToUse: Page shells, readable content boundaries and sections that need a consistent max width.
avoid: Using arbitrary max-width values when a container token fits.
Nesting containers without a deliberate change in content width.
components.accessibility: The default element is a neutral div; choose `as` to provide the correct landmark or section semantics.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render.

props.name: gutter
props.description: Horizontal gutter from the spacing scale. Accepts per-breakpoint values.

props.name: size
props.description: Maximum content width. Accepts per-breakpoint values.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Container size="lg" gutter={{ base: "4", md: "8" }}>Page content</Container>

components.name: Box
components.description: A bordered content region with token-based inset and optional semantic surface.
components.renders: div (or `as`) with token-based inset, optional border and semantic surface
components.composition: Use `size` (`default`, `sm`, `xs`, `xxs`), `surface` (`none`, `card`, `sunken`, `highlight`) and `bordered` to define a content region.
components.whenToUse: A bordered or recessed content area that is not a full Card and does not need Card parts.
avoid: Nesting cards inside cards.
Using Box as a replacement for Stack or Grid.
Using arbitrary backgrounds instead of semantic surfaces.
components.accessibility: The default element is a neutral div; choose `as` when the region has section or landmark semantics.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Whether to show the default border.

props.name: size
props.description: Inset from the spacing scale.

props.name: surface
props.description: Surface inside the box.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: useControllableState
components.renders: no element; returns the current value and a setter
components.composition: Use for controlled/uncontrolled component state. Pass `value`, `defaultValue` and optional `onChange`; domain-specific guards stay in the component.
components.whenToUse: Interactive components that support both controlled and uncontrolled state.
avoid: Using it for state that has no controlled API.
Putting accessibility or domain-specific close/validation rules inside the generic hook.
components.accessibility: The hook renders no DOM and does not replace component-level accessibility behavior.
components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: AspectRatio
components.description:
Reserves space for media with the CSS `asspect-ratio` property. An `img`, `video`, `iframe`,
`picture`, `canvas` or `svg` as a direct child fills the box; images and videos use
`object-fit: cover`. It only renders a `div`: when the media needs a caption, wrap the box
in a `figure` yourself.
components.renders: div
components.composition: Reserves space for media before it loads, preventing layout shift (CLS). `ratio` is width divided by height (`16 / 9`, `4 / 3`, `1`) and defaults to 1. Only `div` is rendered; when the media needs a caption, wrap the box in a `figure` yourself. A direct child `img`, `video`, `iframe`, `picture`, `canvas` or `svg` fills the box; images and videos use `object-fit: cover`.
components.whenToUse: Images, video, embeds or maps whose size must be reserved before they load, preventing layout shift (CLS).
avoid: Text boxes: the box grows with its content.
Decorative containers with no media.
components.accessibility: The child needs its own alt text (`img`) or title (`iframe`, `video`); the box adds no semantics.

props.name: as
props.description:
Element to render. Only `div` is supported: when the media needs a caption, wrap
the box in a `figure` yourself.

props.name: ratio
props.description:
Width divided by height, such as `16 / 9`, `4 / 3` or `1`. The box reserves that area
before the media loads, which prevents layout shift.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.description:
Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree, so screen readers still read it.
Never use `display: none` or `aria-hidden` for this purpose.
components.renders: span (or div)
components.composition: Children only.
components.whenToUse: Text that screen readers must read but sighted users should not see, such as the name of an icon-only button.
avoid: display:none or aria-hidden for this purpose: they remove the content from the accessibility tree.
components.accessibility: Stays in the accessibility tree by design.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <button><Icon .../><VisuallyHidden>Close</VisuallyHidden></button>

components.name: Icon
components.description:
Wrapper for a Phosphor glyph (256x256 grid, filled shapes, `currentColor`).
Do not use it with hand-written paths: import a named icon (`ArrowRightIcon`) instead.
components.renders: svg on a 256x256 viewBox, filled with currentColor
components.composition: Do not pass paths. Import a named icon from the set (CheckIcon, ArrowRightIcon ...) generated by `bun run icons` and listed in /agent/icons.json. Each icon takes `size` (xs 12, sm 16, md 20, lg 24, xl 32) and `weight` (regular | fill). Do not pass `size` to icons inside `startIcon`/`endIcon`; `xs` is for standalone use, inline with text or in small badges.
components.whenToUse: Any glyph. Named icons are decorative by default; pass `label` when the icon is the only carrier of meaning.
avoid: Hand-written <path> children: every icon comes from the generated set.
Meaningful icons without a label.
weight="fill" unless it marks an active or selected state.
components.accessibility: Without `label` it is aria-hidden. With `label` it is role="img" with that name.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name. Provide it when the icon carries meaning on its own (no visible text next to it).
Without `label` the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: size
props.description:
Fixed size: `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px, `lg` 24px, `xl` 32px. Without it the icon is
20px, or the size its parent sets (inside a `Button` it follows the button). `xs` is for
standalone use: inline with text or in small badges.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Icon label="Success">{glyph}</Icon>

components.name: Spinner
components.description:
Indeterminate loading indicator. Twelve thick bars sit around a circle and light up in
sequence, leaving a fading trail that reads as rotation.

Use it only when the wait is expected to last more than a second; for shorter operations it
appears and disappears too fast to help. Use `Skeleton` instead when the shape of the incoming
content is known, and `Progress` when the completion percentage is known.

It paints with `currentColor`, so it inherits the surrounding text color. Announces `label`
through a status region. An empty label makes it decorative: no status role, no hidden text,
and `aria-hidden="true"`. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` by slowing the sequence down.
components.renders: span with role="status" containing twelve decorative bars and VisuallyHidden text, or an aria-hidden span when the label is empty
components.composition: No children. Use `label` to describe what is loading. Sizes: xs 12px, sm 16px, md 20px (default), lg 24px, xl 32px. Paints with currentColor, so it inherits the surrounding text color. An empty label makes it decorative and silent.
components.whenToUse: Indeterminate loading of an action or small region that is expected to take more than a second. Place it next to the content it refers to.
avoid: Waits under a second: it appears and disappears too fast to be useful.
Several spinners announcing at once.
Page-level loading of content shape: use Skeleton.
Known completion percentage: use Progress.
Placing it inside a Button or Badge by hand: use their `loading` prop.
components.accessibility: Announces `label` through a status live region; with an empty label it renders no status role, no VisuallyHidden text and aria-hidden="true". The bars are decorative. Motion follows prefers-reduced-motion by slowing the sequence.

props.name: label
props.description: Text announced to screen readers.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter: `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px, `lg` 24px, `xl` 32px.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Spinner label="Saving changes" />
<Spinner size="sm" label="Uploading" />
<Spinner label="" />

components.name: Skeleton
components.description:
Placeholder for content that is loading. Purely decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology.
Mark the region that is loading with `aria-busy="true"` on its container and announce completion yourself.
components.renders: span (aria-hidden)
components.composition: Shape is text, rect or circle; set width and height with CSS values.
components.whenToUse: Placeholder for content whose layout is known while it loads.
avoid: Using it as the only loading signal.
components.accessibility: Hidden from assistive technology. Put aria-busy="true" on the container that is loading.

props.name: height
props.description: CSS height. Defaults depend on `shape`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape of the placeholder. `text` matches one line of body text.

props.name: width
props.description: CSS width, for example `"12rem"` or `"100%"`.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <section aria-busy="true"><Skeleton width="60%" /><Skeleton shape="rect" height="8rem" /></section>

components.name: Button
components.description:
Action button, or a link when given `href`.

Icon-only controls need an accessible name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
components.renders: button without `href`; a (or the LinkProvider component) with `href`
components.composition: `href` decides the element: a Base UI button (`type="button"` by default) or a link from `LinkProvider` that rejects `disabled`, `loading` and `type`. Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (no `size`). Icon-only needs `startIcon` and one of `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Sizes: xs 1.5rem/12px icon, sm 1.75rem/16px, md 2.25rem/20px, lg 2.75rem/24px. `pill` uses `--radius-full`; inside ButtonGroup only the outer corners keep it.
components.whenToUse: An action with onClick (submit, open, confirm, cancel), or navigation that looks like a button with href. Pass `loading` while an action runs.
avoid: Navigation as inline text: use Link.
onClick plus router.push to navigate: use href, or right-click and new-tab semantics are lost.
More than one primary button per view.
Disabling the button to show progress: use `loading`.
components.accessibility: Icon-only controls need `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) and use `startIcon` instead of children; the types enforce it. `loading` sets `aria-busy` and counts as the start slot, and the spinner stays silent so the button's accessible name is the only announcement. With `href` it is a real link (role link), never role button. Keyboard and disabled behavior on the button branch come from Base UI.

props.name: children
props.description:
The visible label.
Icon-only controls have no visible children.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the control sizes it.

props.name: href
props.description:
Never on an action button. Pass `href` to render a link instead.
Where the link goes. To navigate, pass `href`; do not wire `onClick` to `router.push`, which loses right-click and new-tab semantics.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and ignores clicks while an action is running. The button keeps its label and stays
focusable, and `aria-busy` tells assistive technology it is working.

props.name: pill
props.description: Fully rounded shape (`--radius-full`). Inside `ButtonGroup` only the outer corners keep it.

props.name: size
props.description:
Control height and icon size: `xs` 1.5rem and 12px, `sm` 1.75rem and 16px, `md` 2rem and
20px, `lg` 2.5rem and 24px.

props.name: startIcon
props.description:
Icon before the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the control sizes it.
The visible icon and accessible name. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual emphasis. `primary` is the main action (one per view), `secondary` for other actions,
`ghost` for low-emphasis actions, `accent` for brand emphasis, `danger` for destructive actions.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Button>Save</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="accent" pill>Upgrade</Button>
<Button loading>Saving</Button>
<Button aria-label="Close" startIcon={<XIcon />} />
<Button href="/docs/installation">Get started</Button>

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.description: Joins 2-4 related actions into one control. Children draw their border and radius; the group only zeros the inner edges. It never inherits `size` or `variant`.
components.renders: div role="group"
components.composition: One group of related children: `Button`, a `Menu` trigger, `Input`, `Select` or `ButtonGroupText`. The group does not inherit `size` or `variant`; set both on every child. `stackBelow` stacks it below `sm` or `md`. Children draw the internal 1px line.
components.whenToUse: 2-4 related actions with short labels, all the same size and variant.
avoid: Loose actions that do not form a set.
Unrelated actions.
Long groups: split them or use a Menu.
The `ghost` variant.
components.accessibility: Renders role="group"; add an `aria-label` that names the set of actions. Each child keeps its own accessible name and focus ring, which stays above its neighbours.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
Layout above the `stackBelow` breakpoint. `horizontal` joins the controls side by side;
`vertical` stacks them.

props.name: size
props.description: Shared control size inherited by children that omit their own size.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description:
Stacks the group into a column below this breakpoint and returns to `orientation` above it.
Omit it to keep one orientation at every width.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Document actions">
  <Button variant="secondary">Save draft</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Preview</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Publish</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

parts.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
parts.description: A 1px divider between controls, for a filled variant (`primary`, `accent`, `danger`) that hides the default border; it follows the group's active axis.
parts.composition: A 1px `--color-border-default` line with `align-self: stretch`. Use it when a filled variant hides the default border; it follows the active axis, including `stackBelow`.
parts.whenToUse: Inside a filled group (`primary`, `accent`, `danger`), where the default border is hidden.
avoid: Groups of `secondary` buttons, where the default border already divides.
Decoration outside a ButtonGroup.
parts.accessibility: Exposes role="separator" with an `aria-orientation` that describes the line.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
Direction of the line for assistive technology. The visible line follows the group's active
axis, including `stackBelow`.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Export">
  <Button>CSV</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button>JSON</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

parts.name: ButtonGroupText
parts.description: A static text addon for a `ButtonGroup`, such as `https://` or `USD`, that matches the height of the controls and shares the group border.
parts.composition: Static text only, such as `https://` or `USD`. It matches the height of the controls and shares the group border. No `render`.
parts.whenToUse: A short prefix or unit next to an `Input` or a `Button`.
avoid: Interactive content or actions: use Button.
Long labels: the addon is a short prefix or unit.
Use outside a ButtonGroup.
parts.accessibility: Plain text; it does not add a role or a name. Keep the adjacent control's accessible name complete.

props.name: children
props.description: The addon text, such as `https://` or `USD`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes for the addon surface.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Price">
  <ButtonGroupText>USD</ButtonGroupText>
  <Input aria-label="Amount" inputMode="decimal" />
</ButtonGroup>

components.name: Field
components.description:
Combine labels, controls, and help text to compose accessible form fields and grouped inputs.
Wraps one control with its label, description and error, wired for accessibility by Field
(`label` association, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`). Pass `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and
`loading` here; never wire `aria-describedby` or show a loose red error text by hand. When the
control renders its own label or legend, omit `label`; the control prints Required and keeps its
accessible name.

Errors are shown after the field is blurred or the form is submitted, not on the first keystroke.
components.renders: div containing an optional label, the control, a description and an error
components.composition: Wrap one control: Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch or Slider. `label` is optional: omit it when the control renders its own label or legend (Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider). Pass `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` to Field instead of wiring the control. Controls that carry their own label or legend also accept these props directly.
components.whenToUse: Combine labels, controls, and help text to compose accessible form fields and grouped inputs.
avoid: A loose red error text below the control: use Field `error`.
Wiring aria-describedby or aria-invalid by hand.
components.accessibility: Field wires the label, aria-describedby and aria-invalid; the error is announced politely. `required` sets the native/ARIA required state and prints Required next to the label, or in the control's own label when Field has no label. Errors show after blur or submit, not on the first keystroke (validationMode defaults to onBlur).

props.name: children
props.description:
The control: `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch` or `Slider`.
Controls that carry their own label or legend also accept these validation props directly.

props.name: description
props.description: Help text shown under the control and linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. When set, the field is marked invalid and the message is linked to the control.
Pass an empty string when there is no error. Show it from validation that runs on blur or submit,
not on the first keystroke (Field defaults to `validationMode="onBlur"`).

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label. Required unless the control renders its own label or legend
(Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider).

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a small spinner at the end of the control, marks it `aria-busy`, and makes it not editable.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout with label beside the control. Ignored when `label` is omitted.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
Makes the control read-only: sunken background, no hover, text not dimmed, still focusable and
selectable. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
Marks the control as required and prints "Required" next to the label. The control also gets
`required` so browsers and assistive technology enforce it.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: Return to vertical below this breakpoint (`sm` = 40rem, `md` = 48rem).

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Email" description="We never share it." error={errors.email} required>
  <Input type="email" autoComplete="email" />
</Field>
<Field label="API key" readOnly>
  <Input defaultValue="sk-live-…" />
</Field>
<Field label="Tax ID" loading>
  <Input />
</Field>
<Field error="Turn this on to continue" required>
  <Switch label="Notifications" />
</Field>

parts.name: FieldSet
parts.description: Groups different controls under one accessible legend. Use CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup for same-type options.
parts.renders: fieldset with a legend, optional description and stacked controls
parts.composition: Pass required `legend`, optional `description` and `disabled`, then compose different controls as children. Use CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup for same-type options.
parts.whenToUse: Grouping different controls under one accessible name, such as a shipping address.
avoid: Using it for same-type choices: use CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup.
Grouping unrelated controls.
Using it without a legend.
parts.accessibility: The native fieldset and legend name the group; the description is linked with aria-describedby. Disabled passes to the native fieldset.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: FieldSeparator
parts.description: Divides alternatives between fields, optionally with readable text between the lines.
parts.renders: decorative separator, optionally with readable text between two lines
parts.composition: Place between fields; pass children for text such as `Or continue with`.
parts.whenToUse: Dividing alternatives within a form.
avoid: Using it outside a form: use Separator.
Using it for spacing: use Stack gap.
parts.accessibility: Lines are decorative; children remain readable content when present.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Separator
components.description:
A 1px line that visually or semantically divides content, built on Base UI Separator.
Horizontal by default; use `orientation="vertical"` inside a row. Spacing is not part of the
component: use the parent `gap` or a margin on `className`.
components.renders: div
components.composition: Set `orientation` and `decorative`; it does not accept children. It covers the full width or stretches to the parent height, so size it from the parent. Spacing comes from the parent `gap` or from a margin on `className`.
components.whenToUse: Visually or semantically dividing sections, lists and action groups.
avoid: Using it for spacing: use gap.
Using it inside ButtonGroup: use ButtonGroupSeparator.
components.accessibility: Decorative separators are presentation-only; non-decorative separators expose the separator role and orientation through Base UI.

props.name: decorative
props.description:
Hides the line from assistive technology when true. Set it to false when the line conveys a
real section boundary that screen readers should announce.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Separator />
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<Separator decorative={false} />

components.name: Input
components.description:
A native text input built on Base UI Input. Inside `Field` it is labelled and wired to its
description and error automatically, and it inherits `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
Outside `Field` it needs an accessible name (`aria-label` or an associated `label`).
Icons follow the control size: xs 12px, sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
Styling hooks: set `--input-radius` or `--input-px` on the input wrapper or an ancestor; they
default to `--radius-md` and `--space-3` and are useful when composing with ButtonGroup.
components.renders: input
components.composition: Native input props pass through (type, autoComplete, name, required...). `variant="ghost"` removes resting chrome for low-emphasis fields. Put decorative icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Icons follow the size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
components.whenToUse: Single-line text entry, read-only values and values that are still loading.
avoid: Using it without Field or aria-label.
Multi-line text: use Textarea.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
components.accessibility: Needs an accessible name. Set `autoComplete` for personal data fields. readOnly stays focusable and selectable; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the input sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner at the end and makes the input not editable. `aria-busy` is set.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `xs` 1.5rem, `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2rem, `lg` 2.5rem.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the input sizes it.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual treatment: `ghost` removes the resting chrome for low-emphasis fields.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Email"><Input type="email" autoComplete="email" /></Field>
<Input aria-label="Search" startIcon={<MagnifyingGlassIcon />} />
<Field label="Tax ID" loading><Input /></Field>

components.name: InputOTP
components.description:
Verification code input for four- or six-digit numbers. Typing advances the
focus, backspace and arrow keys move it back, and pasting or the browser's SMS autofill
(`autoComplete="one-time-code"`, the default) fills every slot. Inside `Field` it is labelled by
the Field label and inherits `invalid`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.

The first slot takes the label as its name; the others are named "Character n of N" so a screen
reader says which slot has focus. Outside `Field`, pass `aria-label` for the first slot.

`validationType` is `"numeric"` by default; use `"alphanumeric"` for recovery codes. `mask` hides
the characters, which also turns the slots into password inputs, so password managers may react.
Use `onValueComplete` to verify the code, or `autoSubmit` to submit the owning form.

Styling hook: `--input-radius` (default `--radius-md`).
components.renders: one-time-code input with character slots
components.composition: Use as one component. Set `length`, optional `groups`, `validationType`, `mask` and `onValueComplete` as needed.
components.whenToUse: Verification codes, one-time passwords and recovery codes.
avoid: Splitting it into slot components; Base UI manages slot indexes and focus.
Using it for arbitrary multi-field data entry.
components.accessibility: Inside Field, the first slot uses the Field label and the remaining slots announce their character position. Outside Field, provide aria-label. Loading is read-only with aria-busy=true.

props.name: getSlotLabel
props.description:
Accessible name of each slot after the first, which uses the `Field` label. Pass it to translate
the default "Character 2 of 6".

props.name: groups
props.description:
Splits the slots into visual chunks with a separator between them, e.g. `[3, 3]` for `123-456`.
The numbers must add up to `length`; otherwise they are ignored.

props.name: length
props.description: Number of character slots.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Makes the slots not editable, marks the field `aria-busy` and shows a spinner after the last
slot. Use it while the code is being verified. Inside `Field`, pass `loading` to the Field
instead.

props.name: size
props.description: Slot size: `sm` 2.25rem, `md` 2.75rem.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Verification code" description="Enter the 6 digits we sent you.">
  <InputOTP onValueComplete={verify} />
</Field>
<Field label="Backup code" error={errors.code}>
  <InputOTP length={8} groups={[4, 4]} validationType="alphanumeric" normalizeValue={(v) => v.toUpperCase()} />
</Field>
<Field label="Code" loading>
  <InputOTP />
</Field>
<InputOTP aria-label="Authenticator code" />

components.name: InputGroup
components.description:
Text input with addons (icons, text, buttons, keyboard hints) inside one bordered control.
The border, background, hover, focus ring, invalid, disabled and read-only states live on the group;
`InputGroupInput` is the borderless input inside it. Invalid, disabled, required and read-only come
from `Field` exactly as they do for `Input`.

Put `InputGroupInput` first in the DOM and the addons after it. Visual order comes from `align`, so
keyboard order stays input, then buttons. For a plain icon use `Input` with `startIcon`/`endIcon`.

Styling hooks: `--input-radius` (default `--radius-md`) and `--input-px` (default `--space-3`).
components.renders: div containing one borderless input and optional addons
components.composition: Put `InputGroupInput` first. Add prefixes, units or actions with `InputGroupAddon`.
components.whenToUse: An input with attached text, an icon, a hint or an action.
avoid: Using it just for spacing; use Stack or Grid.
Hiding meaningful units only in an addon.
components.accessibility: Give the input a Field label or aria-label. Icon-only buttons need aria-label.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner after the last addon, marks the input `aria-busy` and makes it not editable.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `xs` 1.5rem, `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2rem, `lg` 2.5rem. Flows to every part.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Search">
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroupInput type="search" />
    <InputGroupAddon><MagnifyingGlassIcon /></InputGroupAddon>
  </InputGroup>
</Field>
<Field label="Website" description="Without the protocol.">
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroupInput />
    <InputGroupAddon><InputGroupText>https://</InputGroupText></InputGroupAddon>
    <InputGroupAddon align="end"><InputGroupText>.com</InputGroupText></InputGroupAddon>
  </InputGroup>
</Field>

parts.name: InputGroupInput
parts.description:
The input of an `InputGroup`: borderless and transparent, with the same text styles as `Input`.
Inherits `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` from the group and `Field`. Needs an accessible name
(`Field label` or `aria-label`).
parts.composition: Use only inside InputGroup. It inherits size, loading, required and readOnly from InputGroup and Field.
parts.whenToUse: The editable control inside InputGroup.
avoid: Using it outside InputGroup; use Input instead.
parts.accessibility: Needs an accessible name from Field or aria-label; loading is read-only with aria-busy=true.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <InputGroupInput aria-label="Amount" inputMode="decimal" />

parts.name: InputGroupAddon
parts.description:
Holds icons, `InputGroupText`, `InputGroupButton` or a keyboard hint beside the input. Icons passed
directly are sized by the group. Text that names the value ("USD", ".com") is not read when the input
is focused, so also say it in the `Field` label or description.
parts.composition: Place after InputGroupInput. Use `align` for its visual side.
parts.whenToUse: Attached icons, text, units, hints or buttons.
avoid: Using addon text as the only place to communicate a unit.
parts.accessibility: Decorative icons are not the input's name; unit text should also appear in the Field label or description.

props.name: align
props.description: Which side of the input it sits on. Visual only; keep it after the input in the DOM.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <InputGroupAddon align="end"><InputGroupText>USD</InputGroupText></InputGroupAddon>

parts.name: InputGroupText
parts.description: Plain text inside an addon: a prefix, suffix or unit.
parts.composition: Use inside InputGroupAddon.
parts.whenToUse: A prefix, suffix or unit.
avoid: Using it as a standalone text style.
parts.accessibility: Repeat meaningful units in the Field label or description.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <InputGroupText>https://</InputGroupText>

parts.name: InputGroupButton
parts.description:
A `Button` sized for the group. Icon-only buttons need `aria-label` (change it when the state
changes, e.g. "Show password" / "Hide password").
parts.composition: Use inside InputGroupAddon. It inherits the group size.
parts.whenToUse: An action tightly attached to an InputGroup, such as clear, copy or show password.
avoid: Using it for unrelated actions; use Button outside the group.
parts.accessibility: Icon-only buttons need aria-label; changing actions such as show/hide password must update the label.

props.name: children
props.description:
The visible label.
Icon-only controls have no visible children.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the control sizes it.

props.name: href
props.description:
Never on an action button. Pass `href` to render a link instead.
Where the link goes. To navigate, pass `href`; do not wire `onClick` to `router.push`, which loses right-click and new-tab semantics.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and ignores clicks while an action is running. The button keeps its label and stays
focusable, and `aria-busy` tells assistive technology it is working.

props.name: size
props.description:
Control height and icon size: `xs` 1.5rem and 12px, `sm` 1.75rem and 16px, `md` 2rem and
20px, `lg` 2.5rem and 24px.

props.name: startIcon
props.description:
Icon before the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the control sizes it.
The visible icon and accessible name. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<InputGroupButton aria-label="Clear" startIcon={<XIcon />} onClick={clear} />
<InputGroupButton variant="secondary">Copy</InputGroupButton>

components.name: Textarea
components.description:
A native `textarea` that works with `Field` the same way `Input` does, including
`required`, `readOnly` and `loading`. Needs an accessible name inside or outside `Field`.
Icons use the 20px medium size (the textarea has no size variants).
components.renders: textarea
components.composition: Native textarea props pass through; `rows` defaults to 3. Put decorative icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
components.whenToUse: Multi-line text entry, including read-only and loading values.
avoid: Using it without Field or aria-label.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
components.accessibility: Needs an accessible name. readOnly stays focusable and selectable; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the textarea sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner at the end and makes the textarea not editable. `aria-busy` is set.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the textarea sizes it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Message"><Textarea rows={4} /></Field>
<Field label="Notes" readOnly><Textarea defaultValue="Locked for review." /></Field>

components.name: Checkbox
components.description:
A checkbox with an optional label, built on Base UI Checkbox. With a label, the whole label is
clickable. Without one, only the box renders: give it a name with `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`
or let `Field` do it. Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
Space toggles it, like a native checkbox.

The dash is only for the `parent` of a `CheckboxGroup`; Base UI derives it from the group.
`variant="card"` turns the label into a card. `invalid` tints the box and label without a
message; `error` adds a linked message. `description` renders help text below the label.
components.renders: span role="checkbox" with a hidden native input, optionally inside a label
components.composition: `variant="card"` turns the label into a card; the dash exists only on the `parent` of a `CheckboxGroup`; `invalid` paints without a message, while `error` adds a message. `label` is optional, but then it needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; `description` adds helper text below the label.
components.whenToUse: Choosing several independent options, or one confirmation that is saved when the form is submitted.
avoid: A single option among several: use RadioGroup.
Settings that apply instantly: use Switch.
Long lists without grouping.
A Card with a Checkbox inside; use `variant="card"`.
components.accessibility: Groups use fieldset and legend; every checkbox without a visible label needs an accessible name. `invalid` tints the label and box; use `error` or Field when the reason should be announced.

props.name: description
props.description:
Help text below the label, linked to it with `aria-describedby`. Inside `Field`, use the
Field `description` instead.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the checkbox invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Marks the checkbox invalid without an error message and tints the label and box with the
danger color. Prefer `error` so the reason is announced; use this only when the label itself
explains the problem. Inside `Field`, pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label, rendered next to the box. In the card variant it fills the card.
Omit the visible label and the wrapping `<label>`; only the box is rendered.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the label, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the checkbox not
interactive.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The checkbox can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken background and keeps
the label text at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The checkbox must be ticked before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required".
Without a visible label there is nowhere to print it: let `Field` show it instead.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual presentation. `card` turns the whole label into a clickable card with a border and
background; use it instead of wrapping a Checkbox in a Card.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Checkbox label="Send me product updates" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Accept terms" error="You must accept the terms" required />
<Checkbox label="Accept the terms" invalid />
<Checkbox label="Email notifications" description="We only email about product changes." />
<Checkbox label="Product updates" description="New features and improvements." variant="card" />
<Checkbox aria-label="Select row 3" />

parts.name: CheckboxGroup
parts.description:
A group of checkboxes that share a name, rendered as a `fieldset` with a `legend` and driven
by Base UI CheckboxGroup. Use `allValues` with a `Checkbox` marked `parent` for a working
"Select all"; the parent goes indeterminate while only some options are ticked.
Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
parts.composition: `legend` is required; children are Checkbox elements. For a working select-all, pass `allValues` to the group and mark one Checkbox as `parent`. Documented under Checkbox parts.
parts.whenToUse: Grouping a short set of related checkboxes under one name.
avoid: One option among several: use RadioGroup.
parts.accessibility: The fieldset and legend name the group; each option keeps its own label.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Checkbox` options.

props.name: legend
props.description: Visible group label, rendered as the `legend` of a `fieldset`. Required: the group needs a name.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the group invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the legend, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the group not
interactive.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The group can be focused and read but not changed. Keeps the options at full contrast.
Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The group must include at least one ticked option before the form can be submitted.
The legend prints "Required". Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<CheckboxGroup legend="Notifications">
  <Checkbox label="Email" value="email" />
  <Checkbox label="SMS" value="sms" />
</CheckboxGroup>
<CheckboxGroup legend="Notifications" defaultValue={["email"]} allValues={["email", "sms"]}>
  <Checkbox label="Select all" parent />
  <Checkbox label="Email" value="email" />
  <Checkbox label="SMS" value="sms" />
</CheckboxGroup>

components.name: RadioGroup
components.description:
A group of mutually exclusive options. Renders a `fieldset` with a `legend`, driven by Base UI
RadioGroup. Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: fieldset with a legend and a radiogroup
components.composition: `legend` is required. Children are Radio elements. Use `description` for group guidance and `orientation` for horizontal layouts. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field; required prints Required in the legend. Radio is documented under Parts.
components.whenToUse: Choosing exactly one option from a short list.
avoid: Long lists: use Select.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys move the selection. The legend names the group. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Radio` options.

props.name: legend
props.description: Visible group label, rendered as the `legend` of a `fieldset`. Required: the group needs a name.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text announced with the group.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the group invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the legend, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the group not
interactive.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout of the options.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The group can be focused and read but not changed. Keeps the options at full contrast.
Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The group must have a selection before the form can be submitted. The legend prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<RadioGroup legend="Plan" defaultValue="free">
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
<RadioGroup legend="Plan" error="Choose a plan" required>
  <Radio value="starter" label="Starter" />
  <Radio value="business" label="Business" />
</RadioGroup>

parts.name: Radio
parts.description:
One option inside a `RadioGroup`, built on Base UI Radio. The whole label is clickable.
Validation state comes from the `RadioGroup` (`error`, `required`, `readOnly`, `loading`).
parts.renders: span role="radio" with a hidden native input, inside a label
parts.composition: Only inside RadioGroup; it is documented under Parts. `value` and `label` are required. Optional `description` adds supporting text and `variant="card"` gives the option a choice-card treatment.
parts.whenToUse: One option of a RadioGroup.
avoid: Using it outside a RadioGroup.
parts.accessibility: The whole label is clickable.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for this option.

props.name: value
props.description: Value submitted and reported when this option is selected.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text shown below the option label.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual treatment of the option.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Switch
components.description:
An on/off switch for a setting that applies immediately, built on Base UI Switch.
For choices that are submitted with a form, prefer `Checkbox`. Inside `Field` it inherits
`error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: span role="switch" with a hidden native input, inside a label
components.composition: `label` is required. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
components.whenToUse: A setting that turns on or off immediately.
avoid: Choices that need a Save button: use Checkbox.
components.accessibility: Announced as a switch with on/off state. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and uses the sunken background; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, rendered next to the switch. Required: every control needs an accessible name.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the switch invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the label, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the switch not
interactive.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The switch can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken background when off and
keeps the label text at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The switch must be on before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Switch label="Dark mode" />
<Switch label="Notifications" error="Turn on notifications to continue" required />

components.name: Select
components.description:
A custom select, built on Base UI Select (keyboard, typeahead, focus and form value come from there).
Pass `items` instead of composing parts; items can include `description` and a `group` heading.
Groups are separated by space and a heading, never by a rule. Long lists keep a compact height
and hide the scrollbar. Inside `Field` it inherits `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
Icons follow the trigger size: xs 12px, sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
The trigger keeps the shared control face while open, including when opened with a mouse.
When used inside `ButtonGroup`, omit `label` and provide `aria-label` so the visible label does
not become part of the group's control row.
components.renders: button role="combobox" with a listbox popup in a portal
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, description?, group?, disabled? }), optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`), and give it `label`, `aria-label` or wrap it in Field. Consecutive items with the same `group` render under a heading, separated from the next group by space, never by a rule. Long lists keep a compact max height and hide the scrollbar. `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Icons follow the trigger size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
components.whenToUse: Choosing one option from a longer list, including read-only and loading states.
avoid: Two or three options: use RadioGroup.
Free text: use Input.
Long lists where users need to type to find an option: use Combobox.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
components.accessibility: Keyboard, typeahead and focus come from Base UI. Needs an accessible name. readOnly prevents choosing another option; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

props.name: items
props.description: The options. Each has a machine `value` and a visible `label`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

props.name: data-force
props.description: Story/test hook: force the focus ring without moving focus.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the value, before the caret. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the select sizes it.

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label. Provide it, or `aria-label`, or put the Select inside `Field`:
every control needs an accessible name.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner at the end and makes the select not editable. `aria-busy` is set.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `xs` 1.5rem, `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2rem, `lg` 2.5rem.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the value. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the select sizes it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Select label="Country" placeholder="Choose one" items={[{ value: "ar", label: "Argentina" }]} />
<Field label="Role" required><Select items={roles} /></Field>

components.name: Modal
components.description:
The root of a modal. Use `role="dialog"` for content and forms, or `role="alertdialog"` for a
decision that interrupts. The parts share one implementation; only the behavior, width and header
color change with props. The page behind stays inert and scroll-locked, focus is trapped and
returned, and Escape closes unless `dismissible` is false.
components.renders: no element: it holds the open state and provides the role (Base UI Dialog.Root, or AlertDialog.Root for role=alertdialog)
components.composition: Structure: Modal > ModalTrigger + ModalContent (title, optional tagline/icon/description, body children, actions). `size` supports xs, sm, md, lg and xl widths; `color` supports neutral, brand, warning and critical and never changes layout. Put one to three actions in `actions`: the safe action first and the primary action last. The form lives in the body; a submit button in the footer targets it with the `form` attribute.
components.whenToUse: Interrupting the user for a decision or a focused task.
avoid: Non-essential information: use inline content, Alert or Tooltip.
Short-lived confirmations: use Toast.
Modals without a title.
components.accessibility: The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description. Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes unless dismissible is false, and the page behind is inert. Alert dialogs require a description and start focus on the safe action.
choosing: Content and forms: Modal with the default role="dialog".
A decision that interrupts: Modal role="alertdialog"; add color="critical" for a destructive action.
Blocking information that needs no form: Modal role="alertdialog".

props.name: children
props.description: `ModalTrigger` and `ModalContent`.

props.name: color
props.description: Tints the header tagline and title. It never changes the panel size or behavior.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the modal starts open when uncontrolled.

props.name: description
props.description:
Description announced as the accessible description. Required for `role="alertdialog"`.
Alert dialogs need a description: it is part of the accessible name and explains the decision.

props.name: dismissible
props.description:
Shows the close button and allows Escape and outside click to close. When false, keep at least one
footer action so the user has a way out.

props.name: onBeforeClose
props.description:
Runs before every close. Return false (or a promise of false) to keep the modal open. Use it to
protect a form with unsaved changes, then open a confirmation with `role="alertdialog"`.
`onOpenChange` is still called once the close is allowed.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state. It covers both opening and closing; there are no separate callbacks.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the modal is open. Use it with `onOpenChange` for a controlled modal.

props.name: returnFocusTo
props.description:
Where focus returns when the original trigger no longer exists. Pass an element ref or an id.
Rare: the trigger is the normal return target.

props.name: role
props.description: Behavior only. Use alertdialog for a decision that interrupts.

props.name: size
props.description: Width of the panel, from the layout width tokens.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Modal role="alertdialog" color="critical" description="This permanently removes the project and its data.">
  <ModalTrigger variant="danger">Delete project</ModalTrigger>
  <ModalContent
    title="Delete project?"
    closeLabel="Close delete confirmation"
    actions={
      <>
        <ModalClose>Cancel</ModalClose>
        <ModalClose variant="danger">Delete</ModalClose>
      </>
    }
  />
</Modal>

parts.name: ModalTrigger
parts.description: The button that opens the modal. It renders a `Button` and inherits the behavior of the root.
parts.composition: Direct child of Modal. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`; use `danger` for the destructive trigger.
parts.whenToUse: The button that opens the modal.
avoid: Using a plain Button to open it.
parts.accessibility: Gets aria-haspopup and expanded state from Base UI.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <ModalTrigger variant="secondary">Open settings</ModalTrigger>

parts.name: ModalContent
parts.description:
The modal panel: header, scrollable body and footer. It reads the role and description from
`Modal`. The footer stacks on mobile with the primary action on top, and sits in one row from
the `md` breakpoint.
parts.renders: div role="dialog" (or role="alertdialog" from the root) in a portal, plus a backdrop
parts.composition: `title` is required and children are the body. `description`, `tagline`, `icon`, `actions` and `closeLabel` are optional. The body scrolls while the header and footer stay visible. Actions stack on mobile with the primary on top.
parts.whenToUse: The panel of the modal.
avoid: Omitting `title`.
Putting the form in the footer instead of the body.
More than three actions.
parts.accessibility: The title is the accessible name; the description is the accessible description. A dialog focuses the first field when the body has a form; an alert dialog focuses the safe action.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button. Keep the copy in the consuming example.

props.name: title
props.description: Modal title. Required: it is the accessible name of the modal.

props.name: actions
props.description: Footer actions: one to three. Put the safe action first and the primary action last.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional body content: text, custom content or a form. It scrolls when it exceeds the available height.

props.name: description
props.description: Explanation announced as the accessible description. Falls back to the `description` on `Modal`.

props.name: tagline
props.description: Optional short label above the title, such as a category or a state.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ModalContent
  title="Invite a teammate"
  closeLabel="Close invite dialog"
  tagline="Workspace"
  actions={<><ModalClose>Cancel</ModalClose><ModalClose>Send invite</ModalClose></>}
>
  <Field label="Email"><Input type="email" /></Field>
</ModalContent>

parts.name: ModalClose
parts.description:
A button that closes the modal. It renders a `Button`. In an alert dialog, mark the safe action
with `initialFocus`; otherwise the first secondary action receives focus.
parts.composition: Inside ModalContent `actions`. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`; use `danger` for the destructive action. Mark the safe action with `initialFocus` in an alert dialog.
parts.whenToUse: Cancel, close and confirm actions.
avoid: Closing by custom onClick state when ModalClose is enough.
parts.accessibility: Closing returns focus to the trigger, or to returnFocusTo when the trigger no longer exists.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: Marks the safe action that receives initial focus in `role="alertdialog"`.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style. Use `danger` for a destructive action.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ModalClose>Cancel</ModalClose>
<ModalClose variant="danger">Delete</ModalClose>

components.name: Tooltip
components.description:
A small label that appears on hover or keyboard focus, built on Base UI Tooltip.
Tooltips do not appear on touch devices and are not a reliable way to describe a control, so use
them only to add clarity (for example the name of an icon button) and never for critical information.
components.renders: the child element as trigger; a popup div in a portal
components.composition: `content` is the text. The single child must be focusable and have its own accessible name.
components.whenToUse: Extra clarity for sighted mouse and keyboard users, such as naming an icon button.
avoid: Essential information: it does not appear on touch and is not linked to the trigger for screen readers.
Interactive content in the tooltip.
components.accessibility: Shows on hover and keyboard focus, hides on Escape. The trigger needs aria-label when it has no text.

props.name: children
props.description:
The element that triggers the tooltip. It must be focusable and already have its own
accessible name (visible text or `aria-label`).

props.name: content
props.description: Short supplementary text. Never put essential information only here.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Opens the tooltip initially.

props.name: open
props.description: Keeps the tooltip open for documentation previews.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Tooltip content="Bold"><Button aria-label="Bold" variant="ghost">B</Button></Tooltip>

components.name: Tabs
components.description:
Tabs that switch between panels, built on Base UI Tabs (arrow-key navigation, roles and
`aria-controls` come from there). Pass `items` instead of composing parts.
Tabs are compact: icons use the 16px small size.
components.renders: div with a tablist, tab buttons and tabpanels
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }) and an `aria-label`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; tabs are compact and use 16px icons.
components.whenToUse: Switching between related panels in the same place.
avoid: Navigation between pages: use Link.
Hiding content users must read.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys move between tabs; roles and aria-controls come from Base UI.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs and their panels, in order.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tab list, for example "Account sections". Required when there is no visible heading for it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
Profile

}, { value: "billing", label: "Billing", content:

Billing

}, ]} />

components.name: Card
components.description:
A bordered container that groups related content into one idea, with a short title.
Its parts share one inset through `--card-spacing`, and an `img` as the first child is
full-bleed with rounded top corners.

Use `as="article"` for self-contained content. If you render a `section`, point
`aria-labelledby` at the `CardTitle`. For state, mark the card with `aria-busy="true"`
while its content loads and let `Skeleton` stand in for the text.
components.renders: div by default; `as` can be article, section or li
components.composition: `CardHeader`, `CardContent` and `CardFooter` are all optional. `size` covers the common insets; set `--card-spacing` on the card for another step of the scale (`--space-5`, `--space-8`). For a full-bleed table, add `data-flush` to `CardContent`. Width is fluid: the container decides it. A link in the title goes as `Link` inside `CardTitle`. For an icon, put an element with `data-card-media` inside `CardHeader`.
components.whenToUse: Grouping related information into a single idea, with a short title.
avoid: Making the whole card clickable: put a `Link` in the title or actions in the footer.
A card inside a card: use `--color-sunken` or an `hr` hairline instead.
Too many actions in the body.
More than one primary CTA.
components.accessibility: Use `article` for self-contained content. The `CardTitle` level follows the page outline.

props.name: as
props.description:
Element to render. Prefer `article` for self-contained content: it can stand alone outside
the page context, with its own heading. If you use `section`, give it `aria-labelledby`
pointing to the `CardTitle` id. `li` only as a direct child of a `ul` or `ol`.

props.name: size
props.description:
Inset between the card edge and its content. `sm` is 1rem, `default` is 1.5rem.
It sets `--card-spacing`, shared by the parts and the gap between them.
An inline `--card-spacing` on the card overrides `size`.

props.name: variant
props.description: `outline` draws only a soft border; `surface` adds the surface fill.
