components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Card as="article" variant="surface">
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Release notes</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>What changed in this version.</CardDescription>
    <CardAction><Button variant="secondary">Share</Button></CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent><Text>Body of the card.</Text></CardContent>
  <CardFooter><Text size="sm" tone="muted">Updated today</Text></CardFooter>
</Card>

parts.name: CardHeader
parts.description:
The top region of a Card: a `CardTitle`, an optional `CardDescription` and an optional
`CardAction` at the top end. A child marked with `data-card-media` (an icon or avatar)
adds a leading column, aligned with the title.
parts.composition: Holds `CardTitle`, optional `CardDescription` and `CardAction`. The action aligns with the title at the top end.
parts.whenToUse: The title region of a Card.
avoid: Using it without a CardTitle.
parts.accessibility: No role of its own; the heading comes from CardTitle.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardTitle
parts.description:
The heading of a Card. Renders a real heading; the default `h3` suits a card inside a section
with an `h2`.
parts.renders: h3 by default; `as` sets the heading element
parts.composition: `as` sets the outline level (h2-h6) and `size` sets the look; it defaults to size 6.
parts.whenToUse: The heading of a Card.
avoid: Skipping heading levels to get a smaller look: change `size` instead.
parts.accessibility: A real heading, so it appears in the document outline.

props.name: as
props.description: Heading level in the document outline. Keep the order of the page.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size from 1 (largest) to 6 (smallest).

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardDescription
parts.description: Supporting text below a `CardTitle`, in the muted body style.
parts.composition: Muted body text below `CardTitle`.
parts.whenToUse: Supporting text directly under the card title.
avoid: Long prose: put it in CardContent.
parts.accessibility: A plain paragraph.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardAction
parts.description: A control at the top end of a Card, aligned with `CardTitle`.
parts.composition: Holds a Button (with `href` for navigation) or Badge at the top end of `CardHeader`, aligned with the title.
parts.whenToUse: A control that belongs to the whole card.
avoid: Hiding the card title to make room for the action.
parts.accessibility: Adds no semantics; the control inside needs its own accessible name.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardContent
parts.description:
The main content region of a Card, aligned with the header and footer.
Add `data-flush` to drop the side inset so the body can reach the card edges,
for example when it holds a `Table`.
parts.composition: The main body between `CardHeader` and `CardFooter`, aligned with both.
parts.whenToUse: The body of a Card.
avoid: Repeating the header or footer content.
parts.accessibility: A plain container.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardFooter
parts.description: The bottom region of a Card, aligned with the header and content.
parts.composition: The bottom region for metadata or actions, aligned with the header and content.
parts.whenToUse: Metadata or closing actions at the bottom of a Card.
avoid: Putting the only primary action at the bottom when CardAction would do.
parts.accessibility: A plain container.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Alert
components.renders: div with role alert (error, warning) or role status (neutral, info, success)
components.composition: Pass `tone` (default `neutral`), an optional `title` and optional content; both can appear alone. `action` reserves space on the right for a `Button size="xs"`; use it with `title`, not with `endIcon`. For several actions, put them in the content. `startIcon` replaces the tone glyph and `endIcon` adds a trailing icon (no `size`). Icon, title, border and background share one tone color; override `--alert-tone` to change it.
components.whenToUse: A message that stays on the page and the user must notice: a general note (neutral), relevant information (info), a completed operation (success), something that needs attention (warning) or a failed operation (error).
avoid: Short-lived confirmations: use Toast.
Using color alone: the tone also changes the icon and you should say it in the text.
Blocking decisions: use Modal role=alertdialog.
Adding visual variants or extra props before a concrete need exists.
`action` without `title`.
`action` together with `endIcon`.
components.accessibility: Announced by screen readers on render. The icon is decorative, and the tone never relies on color alone: the text says what happened.

props.name: action
props.description: A button at the end of the alert, aligned with the title. Reserves space on the right for a `Button size="xs"`; for longer labels or several actions, put them in the content. Use it with `title`, not with `endIcon`.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon at the end, for example a link arrow. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Replaces the tone icon at the start. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: title
props.description: Short heading of the message.

props.name: tone
props.description: Meaning of the message. It changes the icon shape as well as the color, so it never relies on color alone.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Alert title="New dashboard">Take a look at your updated reports.</Alert>

components.name: Avatar
components.description:
A round image of a person with an initials fallback, built on Base UI Avatar.
The whole avatar is one image with the person's name as its label. Add a status or an avatar badge
with an icon inside when needed; without them the markup and accessible name stay just the name.
For bots, companies or systems, use `src` with the logo; without it the initials are shown.
components.renders: span with role img and the name as aria-label
components.composition: Pass `name` (required), `src` and `size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`); initials are the fallback. For bots, companies or systems, use `src` with the logo; without it the initials are shown. `status` adds a solid dot at the bottom end with a page-colored ring and appends the state to the name; `badge` with `badgeLabel` adds an avatar badge with an icon inside and appends its label; `outline={false}` removes the avatar border. `status` and `badge` cannot be combined. Every feature scales with `size`.
components.whenToUse: Showing who a person or account is.
avoid: Using it as a button: wrap it in a Button or Link.
Omitting `name`.
Combining `status` and `badge`: they are mutually exclusive.
components.accessibility: The name is the accessible name. A status appends the state, and an avatar badge appends `badgeLabel`, such as "Ada Lovelace, online" or "Ada Lovelace, Verified". Initials, status dot and avatar badge are hidden from assistive technology; the status is a plain solid dot whose color is not the only signal, because the state is announced in the accessible name.

props.name: name
props.description: Full name of the person or entity. It is the accessible name and the source of the initials. Required.

props.name: badge
props.description: Avatar badge with an icon inside, at the bottom end. Pass a generated icon without `size`. Cannot be combined with `status`.

props.name: badgeLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the avatar badge. Required with `badge`; appended to the accessible name.

props.name: outline
props.description: Whether the avatar keeps its visible border. Set to `false` for a borderless filled circle or image.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter: `xs` 1.5rem, `sm` 2rem, `md` 2.5rem, `lg` 3.5rem, `xl` 4.5rem.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. If it is missing or fails to load, the initials are shown.

props.name: status
props.description: Presence state. Appended to the accessible name, such as "Ada Lovelace, online". Cannot be combined with `badge`.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Stack direction="row" gap="3" align="center">
  <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
  <Avatar name="Grace Hopper" status="online" />
  <AvatarGroup aria-label="Project members">
    <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
    <Avatar name="Grace Hopper" />
    <Avatar name="Alan Turing" />
    <Avatar name="Katherine Johnson" />
  </AvatarGroup>
</Stack>

parts.name: AvatarGroup
parts.description:
Overlapping avatars that share one size, with a page-colored ring so the overlaps stay clean.
When there are more than `max`, the extra avatars collapse into a "+N" item labelled "and N more".
Used outside a group, Avatar is unchanged.
parts.renders: div role="group" with overlapping Avatar elements
parts.composition: Pass `children` (Avatar elements), `max` (default 4) and shared `size` (default md). Avatars overlap by about 25% and each gets a 2px page-colored ring; later avatars stack on top. Avatars beyond `max` collapse into a "+N" item with the component background and label style, labelled "and N more".
parts.whenToUse: A compact summary of several people or accounts.
avoid: One avatar: use Avatar directly.
Long lists where every person matters: show them in a list.
parts.accessibility: The group has role="group"; give it an `aria-label`. Each avatar keeps its own name, and the overflow item is announced as "and N more".

props.name: children
props.description: Avatars in the group. They share the group's `size`.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars stay visible before the rest collapse into a "+N" item.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter shared by every avatar in the group.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<AvatarGroup max={3} aria-label="Project members">
  <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
  <Avatar name="Grace Hopper" />
  <Avatar name="Alan Turing" />
  <Avatar name="Katherine Johnson" />
</AvatarGroup>

components.name: Popover
components.description:
Root of a popover: a small panel anchored to a button, for extra controls or details the user asked for.
Use Popover for about 22rem of content and up to 3–4 fields; use Tooltip for supplementary hints,
Menu for a list of actions, Modal for decisions, and Sheet for longer content.
Built on Base UI Popover (focus management, Escape to close, outside click and positioning come from there).
components.renders: no element: it only holds the open state (Base UI Popover.Root)
components.composition: Structure: Popover > PopoverTrigger + PopoverContent (title required, description optional, PopoverClose). Keep it around 22rem wide with up to 3–4 fields; use Tooltip for supplementary hints, Menu for a list of actions, Modal for decisions, and Sheet for longer content.
components.whenToUse: Small interactive content tied to a button, such as a form or extra options.
avoid: Plain hints: use Tooltip.
Blocking decisions: use Modal.
components.accessibility: Focus moves into the popup and Escape closes it. Title is the accessible name.
components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger variant="secondary">Filters</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent title="Filters" description="Narrow the results.">...</PopoverContent>
</Popover>

parts.name: PopoverTrigger
parts.description: The button that opens the popover. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Child of Popover. Accepts Button props.
parts.whenToUse: The button that opens a Popover.
avoid: Using it outside Popover.
parts.accessibility: A real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: pill
props.description: Fully rounded trigger.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the label, or the icon for an icon-only trigger. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <PopoverTrigger variant="secondary">Filters</PopoverTrigger>

parts.name: PopoverContent
parts.description: The popover panel with its title and description. Place it inside `Popover`.
parts.renders: div with role dialog in a portal, with a title
parts.composition: Child of Popover. Requires `title`; `description`, `side` and `align` are optional.
parts.whenToUse: The panel shown by a Popover.
avoid: Leaving out the title.
parts.accessibility: Labelled by its title. Focus is returned to the trigger on close.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the panel. Required: it is the accessible name of the popover.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment against the trigger.

props.name: children
props.description: The content: text, a form, or `PopoverClose` buttons.

props.name: description
props.description: Short explanation, announced as the accessible description.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<PopoverContent title="Filters" description="Narrow the results.">
  <PopoverClose>Done</PopoverClose>
</PopoverContent>

parts.name: PopoverClose
parts.description: A button that closes the popover. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Inside PopoverContent. Children are the label.
parts.whenToUse: A button that closes the Popover.
avoid: Icon-only without a label.
parts.accessibility: A real button.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <PopoverClose>Done</PopoverClose>

components.name: Menu
components.description:
A dropdown list of actions, links, grouped items, selections and one-level submenus, built on Base UI
Menu (arrow keys, typeahead, focus return and Escape come from there). Items with `href` are real
links; items with `onSelect` are actions. The trigger icons follow its button size; menu items use
clear, 20px icons for better scanability.
components.renders: button that opens a role menu with menuitems
components.composition: Pass `label` (the button text) and `items`: `{ label, startIcon?, endIcon?, onSelect?, href?, disabled?, destructive? }` or `{ type: "separator" }`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; the trigger follows its button size and menu items are compact (16px).
components.whenToUse: A list of actions or links behind one button, such as account actions.
avoid: Navigation between sections of the site: use links.
Form choices: use Select.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys, Home, End, typeahead and Escape come from Base UI. Items with `href` are real links.

props.name: label
props.description: Text of the button that opens the menu.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the menu against the trigger.

props.name: instant
props.description: Removes the popup entrance transition when the menu is coordinated by MenuBar.

props.name: items
props.description: Items in order. Use `{ type: "separator" }` to group them.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a non-interactive loading state inside the popup.

props.name: placement
props.description: Placement relative to the trigger. Overrides `align` when provided.

props.name: singleSelection
props.description: Enables a single-selection radio group for entries with `type: "radio"`.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Optional custom trigger. It must be an accessible button-like element.

props.name: triggerVariant
props.description: Uses a bordered text trigger, like an editor menubar, instead of the default button.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

props.name: width
props.description: Content-sized by default, or one of the fixed semantic menu widths.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Menu label="Account" items={[
  { label: "Profile", href: "/profile" },
  { type: "separator" },
  { label: "Sign out", onSelect: signOut },
]} />

components.name: Accordion
components.description:
Collapsible sections built on Base UI Accordion. Each title is a button inside an `h3`
(`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from Base UI). Pass `items` instead of composing parts.
The plus/minus sign sits at the end: its vertical stroke collapses while opening.
components.renders: div with a heading (h3) and button per item and a region per panel
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, title, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }). Icons are generated icons without `size`. Use `multiple` to allow several open, `disabled` to disable every item and `bordered` for a border around the whole list. To place it inside a Card use `Card` + `CardContent`.
components.whenToUse: Showing long content in short sections, such as FAQs.
avoid: Hiding content users must read.
Navigation between pages.
components.accessibility: Each title is a button in a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, in order.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Draw a border and rounded corners around the whole list, not only between items.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Ids of the panels open at first.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every item. A per-item `disabled` still applies on top.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow several panels open at once.

props.name: value
props.description: Ids of the open panels, when you control it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
Yes.

}, { value: "b", title: "Is it themeable?", content:

Yes.

}, ]} />

components.name: Table
components.description:
Data table with a real `table`, `caption`, `th scope="col"` and a first-column row header. The wrapper
scrolls horizontally on small screens and is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
For layout, use `Grid` or `Stack`, never a table.
components.renders: table with caption, thead, tbody, th scope and a focusable scroll region
components.composition: Pass `caption`, `columns` ({ key, header, align? }) and `rows` (objects by key). Use `align: "end"` for numeric columns: they align end and use tabular numbers.
components.whenToUse: Comparing data across rows and columns.
avoid: Page layout: use Grid or Stack.
Missing caption.
components.accessibility: Real table semantics. The first column is a row header. The scroll wrapper is focusable and named.

props.name: caption
props.description: Describes the table. Required: it is the accessible name and the visible caption.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions, in order.

props.name: rows
props.description: One object per row, keyed by `columns[].key`.

props.name: hideCaption
props.description: Visually hide the caption (it stays available to screen readers).

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Key of the row value that is unique per row. Falls back to the row index.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Table caption="Plans" columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Plan" }, { key: "price", header: "Price", align: "end" }]}
  rows={[{ name: "Free", price: "$0" }, { name: "Pro", price: "$12" }]} />

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description:
Where the current page sits in the site. Renders `nav > ol` and marks the last item with
`aria-current="page"`. Links use whatever `LinkProvider` provides (`next/link` in this app).
components.renders: nav with an ordered list; the last item has aria-current page
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ label, href?, startIcon?, endIcon? }) from root to current page. `separator` defaults to `>` and accepts any node, such as `/` or `·`; it is always hidden from assistive technology. Use `maxItems` (3 or more) to collapse the middle items into an ellipsis menu opened from an icon button labelled Show hidden pages and sized to its content; omit it to show every item. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
components.whenToUse: Hierarchical navigation: showing where a page sits in a site with 3 or more levels.
avoid: Wizards or steps: not a breadcrumb.
Using the current page as a link: it is a span with aria-current="page".
components.accessibility: nav > ol; the nav is labelled Breadcrumb by default; the current page is a span with aria-current="page"; separators are hidden from assistive technology; plain links keep keyboard navigation and a visible focus ring.

props.name: items
props.description: The trail from the root to the current page. The last item is marked as the current page.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation. Change it when a page has more than one breadcrumb.

props.name: maxItems
props.description:
How many items to show before collapsing the middle ones into an ellipsis menu.
Values below 3 are ignored. Omit it to show every item.

props.name: separator
props.description: Node between items. Any node is allowed; it is always hidden from assistive technology.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Components", href: "/docs/components" }, { label: "Button" }]} />
<Breadcrumb maxItems={4} items={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Components", href: "/docs/components" }, { label: "Navigation", href: "/docs/components/navigation" }, { label: "Breadcrumb", href: "/docs/components/breadcrumb" }, { label: "Examples" }]} />

components.name: Pagination
components.description:
Page links for content split across URLs. Every page is a real link, so it works without JavaScript and
with `next/link` through `LinkProvider`. Previous and next are left out (not disabled) when unavailable.
components.renders: nav with a list of links
components.composition: Pass `page`, `pageCount` and `hrefTemplate` such as `/blog?page={page}`. Use `showPreviousNext={false}` for page numbers only, or `showPageNumbers={false}` with `iconSteps` for icon-only Previous and Next.
components.whenToUse: Moving through content split across URLs.
avoid: Passing a function for the href (it breaks in Server Components).
Infinite lists.
components.accessibility: Every page is a link; the current one has aria-current. Previous and Next are removed, not disabled, when unavailable.

props.name: hrefTemplate
props.description: URL of a page, with `{page}` where the number goes, for example `"/blog?page={page}"`. A string (not a function) so it works from Server Components.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, starting at 1.

props.name: pageCount
props.description: Total number of pages.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation.

props.name: iconSteps
props.description: Render Previous and Next as icon-only links.

props.name: showPageNumbers
props.description: Whether to render page-number links and ellipses.

props.name: showPreviousNext
props.description: Whether to render the Previous and Next links.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Pagination page={2} pageCount={9} hrefTemplate="/blog?page={page}" />

components.name: Progress
components.description:
Progress of a task, built on Base UI Progress (`role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`).
For a quick wait with no known end, prefer `Spinner`; for a value the user sets, use `Slider`.
components.renders: div with role progressbar
components.composition: Pass `label` and `value` (number, or null when unknown). Optional `max`.
components.whenToUse: Showing how far a task has got.
avoid: Values the user sets: use Slider.
Short unknown waits: use Spinner.
components.accessibility: role progressbar with aria-valuenow; the label is the accessible name.

props.name: label
props.description: What is progressing. Required: it is the accessible name.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. Use `null` when the amount is unknown (indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the percentage next to the label.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Progress label="Uploading" value={40} />

components.name: Slider
components.description:
Pick a number, or a range, by dragging or with arrow keys. Built on Base UI Slider (each thumb is an
`input type="range"`). For a short list of exact choices use `Select`; for typing a number, use `Input`.
Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: div with one input type range per thumb
components.composition: Pass `label` and `defaultValue` (number or [min, max]). Use `thumbLabels` for ranges and `orientation="vertical"` for a vertical track. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field. Disabled hides the visible label and value; the label remains the accessible name.
components.whenToUse: Choosing a number or range by dragging.
avoid: Exact entry: use Input.
A few named options: use Select.
components.accessibility: Each thumb is a native range input with arrow-key support. The label is the accessible name. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: label
props.description: What the slider sets. Required: it is the accessible name.

props.name: data-force
props.description: Story/test hook: force the focus ring without moving focus.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value, or `[min, max]` for a range.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the slider invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the value, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the slider not
interactive.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Direction of the track. Vertical needs a parent with height, or uses the slider's own height.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The slider can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken track and keeps the
label at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The slider must have a value before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the current value next to the label. Hidden when `disabled`.

props.name: thumbLabels
props.description: Names of the thumbs of a range, for example `["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]`.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value, or `[min, max]` for a range.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Slider label="Volume" defaultValue={40} />
<Slider label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 80]} thumbLabels={["Minimum price", "Maximum price"]} />
<Slider label="Volume" defaultValue={40} orientation="vertical" />
<Slider label="Budget" error="Choose a budget" required />

components.name: Label
components.description:
A visible label for a form control, in the shared `label` text style.
Prefer `Field`, which also wires the description, error and required state.
Use this when you build a custom composition outside Field.
components.renders: label
components.composition: Text children, `htmlFor`, and optional `required` (prints "Required"; the control still needs its own required attribute) and `disabled`. Prefer Field, which wires description, error and ARIA.
components.whenToUse: A visible label for a custom control composition outside Field.
avoid: Replacing Field for a standard form field.
Using it as a heading or body text.
Relying on an asterisk for required: Label spells out "Required".
components.accessibility: Associate it with the control through `htmlFor`. Required state must also be on the control (native or ARIA).
components.callout: For form fields, use Field, which includes built-in label, description, and error handling.

props.name: children
props.description: Text of the label.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the label and removes the pointer cursor. Use only when the control is disabled.

props.name: htmlFor
props.description: The id of the control this label belongs to.

props.name: required
props.description: Prints "Required" after the text. The control still needs its own `required` attribute.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<Label htmlFor="name" required>Name</Label>

components.name: EmptyState
components.description: Explains why a region is empty and how to fill it.
components.renders: section with a labelled heading when `title` is present, otherwise a div
components.composition: Pass required `description`, optional `title`, decorative `illustration`, `actions` (usually one or two Buttons), `size` (`md`, `sm` or `xs`) and `as` for the heading level (`h2`-`h4`, default `h3`).
components.whenToUse: A region without content that needs to explain why it is empty and how to fill it.
avoid: Using it as a generic illustration component.
Adding content beyond illustration, title, description and actions.
Errors or failures: use Alert.
Loading placeholders: use Skeleton.
More than one primary button.
components.accessibility: The illustration is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the description carries the meaning. Vary empty-state text within a page to avoid redundancy for screen readers, and keep it short but meaningful.

props.name: description
props.description: Explains the current situation and, if possible, what to do next. Required. Keep it to one short paragraph.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions that resolve the empty state, usually one or two Buttons. Optional.

props.name: as
props.description: Heading level of the title.

props.name: illustration
props.description: Decorative illustration. Hidden from assistive technology and never shown at size `xs`.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` for screens, tables and large cards; `sm` for cards and panels; `xs` for nested containers.

props.name: title
props.description: Short message that introduces the scenario. Optional.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Sidebar
components.description:
A vertical navigation panel for the side of an app layout. Items can be links or buttons;
links use the component from `LinkProvider`. This is a layout piece, not a Base UI primitive.
components.renders: aside with a nav landmark and a list
components.composition: Pass `label` (required), `items` ({ label, href?, onSelect?, startIcon?, active?, disabled? }), optional `header` and `footer`. Links render with the LinkProvider component; items without href are buttons.
components.whenToUse: Primary vertical navigation beside an app's content, especially on desktop.
avoid: Main site navigation in a header: use SiteHeader or links.
More than one primary sidebar on a page.
Using it for unrelated actions: use Menu or a toolbar.
components.accessibility: The nav landmark is named by `label`; the active item gets aria-current="page". Disabled items are not focusable links and are not clickable.

props.name: items
props.description: The navigation items, in order.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Required.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the navigation, pinned to the end.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the navigation, such as a title or a workspace switcher.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Sidebar
  label="Workspace"
  header={<Heading as="h2" size={6}>Acme</Heading>}
  items={[
    { label: "Overview", href: "/", startIcon: <HouseIcon />, active: true },
    { label: "Settings", href: "/settings", startIcon: <GearIcon /> },
  ]}
/>

components.name: Collapsible
components.description: Root for a single disclosure. Compose it with `CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent`.
components.renders: div with a button trigger and a region panel
components.composition: Pass `title` or a custom `trigger`, panel `children`, optional `startIcon`/`endIcon`, open state (`defaultOpen`, `open`, `onOpenChange`) and `disabled`.
components.whenToUse: A single section that shows or hides content, such as advanced options or extra details.
avoid: Several sections that coordinate: use Accordion.
Content the user must read without interaction.
components.accessibility: The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the panel is its region. Keyboard behavior comes from Base UI. The closed panel remains mounted in the DOM, so descendants such as form fields remain in the document and can be submitted by the surrounding form.

props.name: children
props.description: Content containing a `CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open at first render, when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the trigger.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the open state changes.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CollapsibleTrigger
parts.description: Button that toggles its parent `Collapsible`.
parts.composition: Child of Collapsible. Children are the label; accepts Button props.
parts.whenToUse: The button that shows or hides a Collapsible panel.
avoid: Using it outside Collapsible.
Icon-only without an accessible name.
parts.accessibility: A real button; expanded state and the controlled region come from Base UI.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CollapsibleContent
parts.description: Expandable content for its parent `Collapsible`.
parts.composition: Child of Collapsible. Holds the content that is shown or hidden.
parts.whenToUse: The panel of a Collapsible.
avoid: Using it outside Collapsible.
Hiding content users must read.
parts.accessibility: Labelled by its trigger. The closed panel stays mounted in the DOM.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.description:
A segmented single-choice control built on Base UI Toggle Group. Use it for two to five short,
mutually exclusive options, such as a view switch. For longer content use Tabs; for independent
on/off choices use Checkbox.
components.renders: div role="group" with toggle buttons
components.composition: Pass `label` (required accessible name), `items` ({ value, label, startIcon?, disabled? }), optional controlled value, `size` (sm or md) and `disabled`. Single choice only.
components.whenToUse: Two to five short, mutually exclusive options, such as a view switch.
avoid: Long content changes: use Tabs.
Independent on/off choices: use Checkbox or Switch.
More than five options: use Select.
Related actions that are not a choice: use ButtonGroup.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys move between toggles and roles come from Base UI. The group needs its `label`; selected state is exposed with aria-pressed.

props.name: items
props.description: The options, in order.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the group. Required.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initially selected value, when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the selected value, or an empty string when nothing is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected value, when controlled.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ToggleGroup
  label="View"
  defaultValue="list"
  items={[
    { value: "list", label: "List" },
    { value: "grid", label: "Grid" },
  ]}
/>

components.name: ScrollArea
components.description:
A styled scroll container built on Base UI Scroll Area. Use it for a fixed-height panel, such as
a list or a code area, where the page itself should not scroll. The viewport is keyboard focusable.
components.renders: div frame with a focusable scroll viewport and custom scrollbars
components.composition: Pass `children`, optional `label` (accessible name of the scroll region) and `className` to set the height. Default maximum block size is 12rem; override it with a layout class.
components.whenToUse: A fixed-height list, code area or panel that should scroll inside the page.
avoid: The whole page scrolling: let the page scroll.
Overflowing menus and popups: they handle it themselves.
Horizontal-only swipe carousels with no keyboard alternative.
components.accessibility: The viewport is keyboard focusable and shows a focus ring, so keyboard users can scroll it. Give it `label` when the content is not self-explanatory.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrollable content.

props.name: className
props.description: Class for the outer frame. Use it to set the height.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrollable region.

props.name: viewportClassName
props.description: Class for the scrolling viewport.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ScrollArea label="Activity" className="h-64">
  <Stack gap="3">{items}</Stack>
</ScrollArea>

components.name: Sheet
components.description:
A side sheet for secondary tasks and settings, built on Base UI Drawer. Left and right keep a
fixed side width; top and bottom span the viewport width and fit their content height. Focus is
trapped, Escape closes it, and it can be swiped away on touch. The footer stacks its actions,
and every action fills the available width. For a centered decision use `Modal`.
components.renders: a trigger button; when open, a backdrop and a side panel in a portal
components.composition: Pass `trigger` (button text), `title`, optional `description`, `children`, `footer`, `side` (top, right, bottom or left; default right) and open state. One component, no parts. Left and right use a fixed side width and full height; top and bottom span the viewport width and fit their content height. Footer actions fill the available width and stack when there is more than one. The panel slides and fades on enter (from partial opacity, never 0) and on exit.
components.whenToUse: Secondary tasks, settings and filters that slide in from an edge.
avoid: A centered decision: use Modal.
Non-essential information: use Tooltip or inline content.
Sheets without a title.
components.accessibility: Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes, the page behind is inert, and the title names the sheet. The close button has an accessible label.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button. Keep the copy in the consuming example.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name of the sheet, shown at the top.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Text of the trigger button.

props.name: children
props.description: Main content.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initially open, when uncontrolled.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional explanation under the title.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions shown at the bottom, usually buttons. Each direct child fills the sheet width.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Whether to render the built-in close button.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the sheet enters from.

props.name: triggerSize
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: triggerVariant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Sheet
  trigger="Filters"
  closeLabel="Close filters"
  title="Filters"
  description="Narrow the results."
  footer={<Button>Apply</Button>}
>
  <Field label="Status"><Select items={statuses} /></Field>
</Sheet>

components.name: Combobox
components.description: Searchable single- or multi-choice field. Labels come from `Field`.
components.renders: input role="combobox" with a filterable listbox popup
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, description?, group?, startIcon?, disabled? }). `multiple` shows chips. `clearable` shows a button to clear the selection. `icon` is the end icon: omit for the caret, `null` to hide. Label through Field, or `aria-label`.
components.whenToUse: Choosing from a long list where typing to filter helps, or choosing several values.
avoid: Short lists or no typing needed: use Select.
Two or three options: use RadioGroup.
Binary choices: use Checkbox or Switch.
Free text with no fixed options: use Input.
components.accessibility: Enter or Arrow Down opens; Arrow Up/Down navigate; Enter selects; Escape closes; Backspace removes the last chip in multiple mode. Keyboard, filtering and ARIA come from Base UI.

props.name: items
props.description: The options. Each has a machine `value` and a visible `label`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no `Field` label.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Shows a button to clear the selection.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Text shown when the filter matches nothing.

props.name: icon
props.description: End icon. Omit for the caret, `null` to hide it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner and blocks editing. Inside `Field`, pass it to the Field.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem, `lg` 2.75rem.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.description:
Preformatted code with syntax highlighting, an icon-only copy button and optional tabs for
alternatives such as bun, pnpm and npm. Colors come from semantic `--syntax-*` tokens, so light
and dark work without extra code. Unknown languages are shown as plain text.
components.renders: server component that highlights with Shiki, wrapped around a client view with an icon-only copy button, optional tabs and a focusable region
components.composition: Pass `code` and a `language`. `tone` is `default`, `brand`, `success` or `danger`; `highlight={false}` shows plain text; `highlightLines` marks lines from 1; `lineNumbers` shows decorative line numbers. For alternatives, pass `tabs` instead of `code`.
components.whenToUse: Showing code or commands the user will copy.
avoid: Long documents.
Inline code: use Kbd or a code element.
Expecting syntax color for unsupported languages.
components.accessibility: The code region is focusable with a `label`; line numbers are decorative and the copy result is announced via role status.

props.name: code
props.description: The code to show, as plain text. Use `tabs` instead when there are alternatives (bun, npm, pnpm).

props.name: highlight
props.description: Highlight known languages on the server. Unknown languages fall back to plain text.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description:
1-based line numbers to mark with a 2px left bar and a subtle background. No line numbers are
rendered. The same lines apply to every tab.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrollable code region.

props.name: language
props.description: Language name: bash, css, diff, html, json, ts or tsx; aliases include sh, shell, zsh, js, javascript and jsx.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Show decorative, non-copyable line numbers.

props.name: minimal
props.description: Render only the code with a copy action overlaid at the trailing edge.

props.name: tabs
props.description: Alternative versions of the same code, usually one command per package manager. The first tab is selected first.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color the frame for the kind of message: default, brand, success or danger.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CodeBlockView
parts.description:
Presentation half of `CodeBlock`: tabs, copy button and the focusable code region.
The server passes highlighted HTML; without it the code stays plain text.
parts.renders: client-only presentation of a CodeBlock: tabs, copy button and focusable code region
parts.composition: Internal to CodeBlock. Use it only in client components; pass pre-highlighted `html`/`tabHtml` when available, otherwise the code stays plain.
parts.whenToUse: Client components that cannot render the server CodeBlock.
avoid: Server pages: use CodeBlock, which highlights automatically.
Coloring tokens by hand.
parts.accessibility: The code region is focusable and named; the copy result is announced via role status.

props.name: code
props.description: The code to show, as plain text. Use `tabs` instead when there are alternatives (bun, npm, pnpm).

props.name: highlightLines
props.description:
1-based line numbers to mark with a 2px left bar and a subtle background. No line numbers are
rendered. The same lines apply to every tab.

props.name: html
props.description: Highlighted HTML for `code`, produced on the server.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrollable code region.

props.name: language
props.description: Language name: bash, css, diff, html, json, ts or tsx; aliases include sh, shell, zsh, js, javascript and jsx.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Show decorative, non-copyable line numbers.

props.name: minimal
props.description: Render only the code with a copy action overlaid at the trailing edge.

props.name: tabHtml
props.description: Highlighted HTML per tab label, produced on the server.

props.name: tabs
props.description: Alternative versions of the same code, usually one command per package manager. The first tab is selected first.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color the frame for the kind of message: default, brand, success or danger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

foundations.name: Heading
foundations.description:
A heading. Separates semantics (`as`) from appearance (`size`). Headings are always upright and semibold.
When `id` is omitted, a stable slug of the text is used, so anchors render the same on the server and the client.
foundations.composition: `as` sets the outline level (h1-h6 only); `size` sets only the look.
avoid: Skipping levels (h1 then h3).
More than one h1 per page.
Choosing a level for its look: change `size` instead.
foundations.accessibility: Heading order is part of the page structure for screen reader users.

props.name: as
props.description: Heading level in the document outline. Keep one `h1` per page and do not skip levels.

props.name: size
props.description:
Visual size from 1 (56px) to 6 (20px) on wide screens. Defaults to the size that matches `as`.
Use it to get an `h2` that looks like a size 4.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight. There is no light; headings are semibold unless you set another.

foundations.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Heading as="h1">Page title</Heading>
<Heading as="h2" size={4}>Smaller-looking section title</Heading>

providersAndHooks.name: LinkProvider
providersAndHooks.description:
Wires navigation once for the whole app. In Next.js pass `next/link` so every library link gets
client-side navigation and prefetching, with no `render` prop on each one. Without it links are plain `a` elements.
providersAndHooks.renders: no element: it provides the link component through context
providersAndHooks.composition: Place once near the app root: `<LinkProvider component={NextLink}>`. Link, Button with href, Menu link items, Breadcrumb and Pagination then render with it.
providersAndHooks.whenToUse: Making every link in the library use `next/link` (or another router link) from a single place.
avoid: Passing a `render` prop to individual links.
Nesting several providers.
providersAndHooks.accessibility: No effect on semantics; the provided component must render an `a`.

props.name: component
props.description: The component every `Link`, `Breadcrumb`, `Pagination` and `Menu` link renders with. Pass `next/link` in a Next.js app.

providersAndHooks.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

providersAndHooks.name: TooltipProvider
providersAndHooks.description:
Shares the open delay between tooltips. The first tooltip waits `delay` ms; moving to the next
one opens instantly (`data-instant` skips the animation). Put it once near the app root.
providersAndHooks.composition: Place once near the app root. Optional. `delay` (default 600) applies only to the first tooltip; the next ones open instantly.
avoid: Nesting several providers.
providersAndHooks.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

providersAndHooks.name: ToastProvider
providersAndHooks.description:
Place once near the root of the app (inside `Providers`). It renders the stack of toasts and makes
`useToast` available. Built on Base UI Toast (live-region announcements, F6 to reach the toasts, swipe to
dismiss, pause on hover and focus come from there).
providersAndHooks.renders: no visible element until a toast is shown; renders a viewport in a portal
providersAndHooks.composition: Place once near the app root, inside Providers. Then call `useToast()` anywhere below it.
avoid: Messages that must stay: use Alert.
Several providers.
providersAndHooks.accessibility: Live-region announcements, F6 to reach toasts, pause on hover and focus. The dismiss button is labelled.
providersAndHooks.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <ToastProvider>{children}</ToastProvider>

providersAndHooks.name: useLinkComponent
providersAndHooks.description: The anchor component to render links with: the one from `LinkProvider`, or `a`.
providersAndHooks.composition: Only needed when building your own link components that should respect LinkProvider. `const LinkEl = useLinkComponent()` returns the provided link component, or `"a"`.
providersAndHooks.whenToUse: Building your own navigation component that should follow LinkProvider.
avoid: Calling it in Server Components: it needs a client component.
providersAndHooks.accessibility: The returned component must render an `a`.
providersAndHooks.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

providersAndHooks.name: useToast
providersAndHooks.description:
Show short-lived feedback after an action (saved, copied, failed). Returns `show` and `close`.
For messages that must stay on the page, use `Alert`.
providersAndHooks.composition: `const { show, close } = useToast(); show({ title, description?, tone?, timeout?, startIcon?, endIcon? })`. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
providersAndHooks.whenToUse: Showing a toast after an action finishes.
avoid: Calling it outside ToastProvider.
Putting the only copy of important information in a toast.
providersAndHooks.accessibility: The tone is never the only signal: write it in the title.
providersAndHooks.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
const { show } = useToast();
show({ title: "Saved", tone: "success" });
